Rashi on Chullin 68a:11:1.hebrew: הא נמי תנינא - בבהמה נמי תנינא במתניתין בפירקין דראש הוי לידה, דקתני: "שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסורה באכילה", אפילו מה שהיה בפנים בשעת שחיטה; לפי שהשליא סימן ולד באשה וסימן ולד בבהמה, וחיישינן דלמא בההיא מקצת דנפיק יצא הראש והוי כילוד, הלכך כולה אסורה, דשדינן לה בתר רישא; אלמא ראשו תנן דהוי לידה, וסיפא דקתני "החזירו" לא אצטריך:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:11:1.english: We have also learned this - Regarding an animal as well, we have learned in the Mishnah in our chapter that [the emergence of] the head constitutes birth, as it teaches: "A placenta that emerged partially is prohibited to be eaten," even [the part] that was inside [the womb] at the time of slaughter; because a placenta is a sign of a fetus in a woman and a sign of a fetus in an animal, and we are concerned lest the head emerged in that partial [portion] that came out, and [thus] it is [considered] as born. Therefore, all of it is prohibited, as we assign it after the beginning [that emerged]; thus, we have [already] learned [regarding] its head that it constitutes birth, and the latter clause [of our Mishnah], which teaches "[if] he returned it," is unnecessary:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:12:1.hebrew: א"א בשלמא החזירו דרישא דוקא - ולמישרי אבר גופיה, איכא לתרוצי סיפא דתני "החזירו" משום רישא; אלא אי אמרת "מותר" דרישא אעובר קאי, אבל אבר אסור דחזרה לא מהני — אמאי נקט "החזירו":
Rashi on Chullin 68a:12:1.english: Granted, if you say [that] "it brought [its foreleg] back" of the first clause is specific - and [is meant] to permit the limb itself, one can explain the latter clause — which teaches "it brought [it] back" — [as having been taught] because of the first clause; but if you say [that] "permitted" of the first clause refers to the fetus, whereas the limb is forbidden because returning [it] is not effective — why did [the Mishnah] state "it brought [it] back"?

Rashi on Chullin 68a:14:1.hebrew: לעולם - "מותר" דקתני, אעובר; ודקשיא לך: חזרה מאי אהני? למקום חתך מהניא — דאם לא החזיר, צריך להניח ממה שבפנים לצד החיצון ולחותכו, שמקום החתך — הבדלת החיצון והפנימי — אסור, מפני שהוא עומד על שפת הרחם, ולא קרינא ביה "בהמה בבהמה", דלאו בתוכה הוא. אבל החזירו — א"צ לחתוך לצד פנים, אלא מצמצם וחותך, ומקום חתך מותר, דקרינא ביה "בהמה בבהמה", ומשום "בשר בשדה" ליכא, דהא לא יצא ממחיצתו. והא דרב נחמן — לקמן:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:14:1.english: Actually - [the word] "permitted" that [the Mishnah] teaches [refers] to the fetus; and as for your difficulty: what does bringing [the limb] back accomplish? It accomplishes [something] with regard to the place of the cut — for if [the fetus] did not bring [it] back, one must leave [some] of what is inside toward the outer side and cut it [off], because the place of the cut — the division between the outer and the inner — is forbidden, since it stands at the edge of the womb, and we do not apply to it [the verse] "an animal within an animal," as it is not within it. However, if it brought it back, one does not need to cut toward the inner side; rather, one cuts right at the exact [boundary], and the place of the cut is permitted, since we apply to it "an animal within an animal," and there is no [prohibition] on account of "flesh in the field," since it did not go out of its enclosure. And this [statement] of Rav Nachman [appears] below:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:16:1.hebrew: שבחוץ טמא - דילפינן בהעור והרוטב (לקמן חולין דף קכח:) שאבר מן החי מטמא כאבר מן הנבלה, מ"וכי ימות מן הבהמה":
Rashi on Chullin 68a:16:1.english: That which was outside is ritually impure - because we derive in [the chapter] HaOr VeHaRotev (later, Chullin 128b) that a limb [severed] from a living animal imparts ritual impurity like a limb from a carcass, from [the verse] "And if [an animal] of the beasts dies":

Rashi on Chullin 68a:16:2.english: [That] which was inside is ritually pure - because while alive it did not contract food impurity:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:1:1.english: An animal encountering difficulty giving birth - [that is,] at the time of slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:1:2.english: And brought it back - prior to slaughter:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:1:3.english: Permitted to be eaten - And in the Gemara it explains what is permitted:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:1:4.hebrew: הרי זה כילוד - ותו לא מהניא ליה שחיטת אמו, וצריך שחיטה לעצמו אם נמצא חי, ואם נמצא מת, הרי הוא כנבלה:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:1:4.english: This [fetus] is like a newborn - and the slaughter of its mother is no longer effective for it, and it requires its own slaughter if it is found alive, and if it is found dead, it is like a carcass [neveilah].

Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:1.english: [If one] severs from a fetus that is in its womb - and left the piece inside it:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:2.hebrew: מותר - בשחיטתה, כדיליף בגמרא מ"כל בבהמה תאכלו":
Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:2.english: [It is] permitted - through its [the mother's] slaughter, as derived in the Gemara from "all in an animal you may eat":

Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:3.english: From the spleen or from the kidneys - of the animal itself:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:4.hebrew: אסור באכילה - ואע"פ שהניחו בבהמה, לא הותר בשחיטתה. להכי נקט טחול וכליות, משום דמידי דלא מיטרפא הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:2:4.english: Its consumption is prohibited - Even though he left it inside the animal, it is not permitted by its slaughter. This is why [the Mishnah] specifically mentioned spleen and kidneys: because it is something [whose removal] does not render [the animal] a tereifah:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:3:1.hebrew: ואבר עצמו אסור - באכילה, מאחר שיצא ממחיצתו קודם שחיטה, ואע"פ שהחזירה קודם לכן:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:3:1.english: And the limb itself is prohibited - for consumption, since it exited its partition [the womb] before slaughter, even though [the fetus] brought it back inside before then:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:4:1.hebrew: ובשר בשדה - כלומר, חוץ למחיצתו, דהיינו לאויר, שרחם זה הוה ליה מחיצה להתירו בשחיטה, וכיון שיצא הרי הוא כטרפה ולא תאכלו. וכל מי שיש לו מחיצה ויצא, כגון בשר קדשים שיצאו, נמי מהאי קרא נפקא לן (מכות דף יח.):
Rashi on Chullin 68a:4:1.english: And flesh, in the field - That is to say, outside of its boundary, which means into the [open] air; for this womb served as a boundary for it to permit it through [its mother's] slaughter, and once it has gone out, it is like a tereifah and "you shall not eat [it]." And anything that has a boundary and goes out [of it] — such as sacrificial meat that went out [of its permitted area] — is also derived from this verse (Makkot 18a):

Rashi on Chullin 68a:5:1.english: No, [it refers] to the fetus - And [the Mishnah] teaches us that because of a foreleg, it is not considered as born:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:6:1.hebrew: אפי' לא החזירו נמי - דעובר נפקא לן לקמן מ"בהמה בבהמה אותה תאכלו":
Rashi on Chullin 68a:6:1.english: Even [if] it did not bring it back as well - For [the permissibility of] a fetus is derived by us below from "an animal within an animal, it you may eat":

Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:1.hebrew: וסיפא - גופה מאי קמ"ל, דקאמרת רישא תני משום סיפא:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:1.english: And the latter clause - itself, what does it teach us, since you say [that] the first clause was taught because of the latter clause:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:2.hebrew: בכור לנחלה - בעינן ולד שיהא ראוי לחיות, ואי לא ראוי לחיות — לא מפקע את הבא אחריו מליטול פי שנים, דכתיב (דברים כ״א:י״ז): "ראשית אונו" — מי שלבו דוה עליו, יצא ולד שאינו של קיימא, שאין לב אביו דוה על מותו; אבל מפדיון הבכור פוטר הוא את הבא אחריו, שהרי זה פטר את הרחם:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:2.english: A firstborn with regard to inheritance - We require a child that is viable, and if it is not viable, it does not prevent the one who comes after it from taking a double portion, as it is written (Deuteronomy 21:17): "the firstfruits of his strength" — [meaning] one over whom his [father's] heart grieves, excluding a non-viable child, over whose death his father's heart does not grieve. However, from the redemption of the firstborn, it does exempt the one who comes after it, since this one [indeed] opened the womb:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:3.english: A non-viable fetus [nefel] - [one] whose months [of gestation] were not completed:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:4.hebrew: אע"פ שיצא ראשו חי - והחזירו, ויצא אחיו שכלו חדשיו, אין לידת הראשון מפקעתו מלהיות בכור לנחלה, שאפילו נולד הנפל כולו אינו מפקיע את הבא אחריו, שאין לבו דוה עליו, וכל שכן אם יצא ראשו מת. והאי דנקט "ראשו", משום בכור לכהן נקט ליה, וביציאת ראשו הוי ילוד, ופוטר את אחיו מבכור לכהן:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:4.english: Even though its head emerged alive - and it withdrew it, and its brother whose months [of gestation] were completed emerged [first], the birth of the first does not disqualify him from being a firstborn for inheritance, for even if the non-viable fetus were born completely, it does not disqualify the one who comes after it, since [the father's] heart does not grieve over it, and all the more so if its head emerged dead. And that which [the Mishnah] stated "its head," it stated it because of [the law of] a firstborn [with regard] to a kohen, for through the emergence of its head it is considered born, and it exempts its brother from [being] a firstborn [with regard] to a kohen:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:5.hebrew: או - הבא אחר בן תשעה, אפי' יצא ראשו של ראשון מת, הויא לידת הראשון לידה ואין הבא אחריו בכור לכהן; אבל הבא אחר בן תשעה שיצא ראשו חי, בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי. אלמא ראש הויא לידה:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:7:5.english: Or - [one who] comes after a nine[-month fetus]: even [if] the head of the first emerged dead, the birth of the first is [considered] a birth, and the one who comes after it is not a firstborn with regard to the Kohen; however, [one who] comes after a nine[-month fetus] whose head emerged alive is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance either. Thus, [the emergence of] the head is [considered] a birth:

Rashi on Chullin 68a:9:1.hebrew: וכי תימא אשמועינן באדם - דביציאת ראשו הוי כילוד, והדר אשמועי' בבהמה, דאדם מבהמה לא יליף: דבהמה לית לה פרוזדור לפני בית הרחם שלה, וגלוי הוא, ומכיון שהראש יוצא, לידתו ניכרת; אבל אשה, אין רחמה בגלוי, שהירכים הוו לה כעין פרוזדור, ואין יציאת הולד ניכרת יפה עד שיצא רובו:
Rashi on Chullin 68a:9:1.english: And if you would say it taught us regarding a person - that upon the emergence of its head it is [considered] as born, and then it taught us regarding an animal, because a person cannot be derived from an animal: for an animal does not have a vestibule in front of its womb, and it is exposed, so once the head emerges, its birth is discernible; whereas a woman's womb is not exposed, for the thighs serve for her as a kind of vestibule, and the emergence of the fetus is not clearly discernible until most of it emerges:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:10:1.hebrew: אדם מבהמה לא יליף דאין פרוזדור לבהמה - האי פרוזדור דהכא לא הוי כי ההוא דיוצא דופן (נדה דף מב:), דאמר דמכי הוציא ולד ראשו חוץ לפרוזדור הוי כילוד; דאי כפרוזדור דהתם איירי הכא, מה היה יכול הפרוזדור לעכב הלידה, כיון שהראש חוצה לו? אלא, פרוזדור דהתם הוא בית החיצון, ודהכא הוא עובי הירכים המכסים את הרחם שבין הירכים, כדפ"ה, ומש"ה לא חשיב כילוד ביציאת ראש חוץ לרחם. ואין תימה על שהלשון שוה והפירוש משתנה, דכי האי גוונא אשכחן בפ' הלוקח בהמה (בכורות דף כ.), דאמר רבי [יהושע]: טינוף פוטר מבכורה, דחשיב הטינוף ולד; ולא הוי ההיא טינוף ולד כי האי דפ' המפלת (נדה דף כט.), דרוב יולדות מטנפות:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:10:1.english: A person cannot be derived from an animal, as an animal does not have a prozdor - This prozdor [mentioned] here is not like that [mentioned in the chapter entitled] Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 42b), where it says that once a fetus has put its head out beyond the prozdor, it is considered as born; for if it were speaking here of the prozdor [mentioned] there, how could the prozdor delay [the status of] birth once the head is outside of it? Rather, the prozdor [mentioned] there is the outer chamber [of the birth canal], whereas [the one mentioned] here is the thickness of the thighs that cover the womb between the thighs, as the Master [Rashi] explained; and therefore it is not considered as born upon the emergence of the head outside the womb. And it is not surprising that the terminology is the same while the meaning changes, for we find [a case] like this in the chapter [entitled] Halokeach Behemah (Bekhorot 20a), where Rabbi [Yehoshua] says: Discharge exempts [an animal] from [the law of] the firstborn, because the discharge is considered a fetus; yet that discharge [called] "fetus" is not like that [discharge mentioned] in the chapter [entitled] Hamapelet (Niddah 29a), [where it says] that most women giving birth have a discharge:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:11:1.hebrew: שליא שיצתה מקצתה אסור באכילה - אפי' מה שהיה בפנים בשעת שחיטה. וא"ת: היכי מוכח מיניה דבראש הוי כילוד? דלמא משום דגזרינן מקצתה, דמהא נמי דחי לה בפ"ק דב"ק (דף יא.), דקאמר אמילתא דרבי אלעזר: מאי קא משמע לן, דאין מקצת שליא בלא ולד? תנינא: שליא שיצתה מקצתה כו'. וי"ל: דאם איתא דביציאת הראש לא הויא לידה, לא היה ראוי לגזור, כיון דבמקצתה אי אפשר בשום פעם לבא לידי חשיבות לידה. ומהכא ליכא למפרך לשמואל, דאמר בפ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מו:) דאין הראש פוטר בנפלים; דדילמא היינו דוקא בבהמה, אבל באדם לא שמעינן מהכא, דהא דקתני סיפא "כסימן ולד באשה כך סימן ולד בבהמה", היינו לענין שליא, דהוי סימן ולד:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:11:1.english: A placenta that emerged partially is prohibited for consumption - Even that which was inside at the time of slaughter. And if you ask: How is it proven from it that through [the emergence of] the head [the fetus] is considered born? Perhaps it is because we make a decree [regarding] part of it [due to all of it], for from this [very reasoning] [the Gemara] also refutes [the proof] in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (11a), where it says regarding the statement of Rabbi Elazar: "What does he teach us — that there is no part of a placenta without a fetus? We have learned: A placenta that emerged partially, etc." And one can answer: If it were so that with the emergence of the head it is not [considered] a birth, it would not be fitting to make a decree, since in [the case of] part of it [emerging] it is never possible to come to the status of birth. And from here one cannot raise a difficulty against Shmuel, who says in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 46b) that the [emergence of the] head does not exempt [a subsequent birth from firstborn status] in the case of non-viable births; for perhaps this [rule that the head is considered birth] applies specifically to an animal, whereas regarding a human we do not learn [it] from here, for that which the latter clause teaches, "Just as [it is] an indication of a fetus in a woman, so [is it] an indication of a fetus in an animal," refers [only] to the matter of the placenta, that it is an indication of a fetus:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:11:2.hebrew: כסימן ולד באשה כך סימן ולד כו' - וא"ת: מאי פשוט יותר בזה מבזה? וי"ל: משום דתנן בנדה (דף כה.) דבאשה הוי שפיר סימן ולד, לכך קאמר דאע"ג דבבהמה לא הוי שפיר סימן ולד, מ"מ בשליא שוה לאשה:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:11:2.english: Just as [it is] an indication of a fetus in a woman, so too [is it] an indication of a fetus, etc. - And if you ask: Why is [it] more obvious in this [case] than in that [case]? And one can answer: Because we learned in [tractate] Niddah (25a) that in a woman a *shafir* [amniotic sac] is an indication of a fetus, therefore [the mishna] says that even though in an animal a *shafir* is not an indication of a fetus, nevertheless, with respect to a placenta, it is equal to a woman:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:4:1.hebrew: כיון שיצא בשר חוץ למחיצתו נאסר - כדדריש לקמן, דומיא דטרפה דאין לה היתר:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:4:1.english: Once flesh has gone outside of its boundary, it becomes prohibited - As [the Gemara] expounds later, similar to a tereifa, which has no [way to become] permitted:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:7:1.hebrew: סיפא מאי קמ"ל דכיון שיצא ראשו הויא לידה תנינא - וא"ת: ודילמא איצטריך לאשמועינן אע"ג דהחזירו הוי כילוד, דמההיא דבכורות לא שמעינן אלא בלא החזירו? וי"ל, דפשיטא ליה דכיון דבלא חזרה הויא לידה, כי החזירו נמי לא כלום הויא. ומיהו אי לאו ההוא דבכורות, לא הויא קשיא ליה אמאי איצטריך ליה למיתני "החזירו", דכיון דאצטריך לאשמועי' דיציאת ראש הויא לידה, אשמועינן נמי אגב אורחיה דחזרה לאו כלום הוא; אבל כוליה בבא לית ליה למיתני משום האי חידוש פורתא. וזה נמי אין להקשות: דהכא אצטריך לאשמועינן דאפי' מה שבפנים אסור — דלרב יהודה "אסור" קאי אעובר — והא לא שמעינן מההיא דבכורות; דהא נמי פשיטא, דכיון דחשיב כילוד, ואפי' מה שבפנים אסור כיון שהולד שלם; ובנחתך הוא דמיבעיא ליה לקמן, כמו שאפרש לקמן בעזרת האל:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:7:1.english: What does the latter clause teach us? [Does it teach] that once its head emerged, it is [considered] a birth? We have [already] learned this - And if you will say: Perhaps [the Mishnah] was needed to teach us that even though [the fetus] retracted it, it is considered as born, for from that [mishna] in Bekhorot we only learn [the case] where it did not retract it? And one can say: It is obvious to [the Gemara] that since without retraction it is [considered] a birth, when it retracted it as well, [the retraction] is nothing. However, were it not for that [mishna] in Bekhorot, [the Gemara] would not have found it difficult why [the Tanna] needed to teach "and retracted it"; for since [the Tanna] needed to teach us that the emergence of the head is [considered] a birth, he also taught us incidentally that retraction is nothing — but he would not have taught an entire clause [just] for this slight novelty. And this too cannot be asked: that here [the Mishnah] was needed to teach us that even what is inside is forbidden — for according to Rav Yehuda, "is forbidden" refers to the fetus — and this we do not learn from that [mishna] in Bekhorot; for this too is obvious, that since it is considered as born, even what is inside is forbidden since the fetus is whole; and it is [only] regarding [when the fetus is] cut up that [the Gemara] raises a dilemma below, as I will explain below with the help of God:

Tosafot on Chullin 68a:8:1.hebrew: טעמא דראשו מת הא ראשו חי כו' - תימה, דהוה ליה למפרך בפשיטות מדקתני "ואין בכור לכהן", א"כ מכי יצא ראשו הוי כילוד! וי"ל, משום דאיכא למדחי: מאי "ראשו"? רובו, כדדחי בפ' יש בכור (בכורות מו:), דאמר שמואל: אין הראש פוטר בנפלים, ופריך ליה מהא ד"אין בכור לכהן", ומשני: מאי "ראשו"? רובו — פירוש: יצא ראשו וגם יצא רובו אח"כ; ופריך: וניתני "רובו"! ומשני: דנקט "ראשו" למידק הא ראשו חי, בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי. הלכך עיקר פרכיה מהאי דיוקא. והוה מצי למיפרך הכא ממתני' דנדה, דתנן (דף כח.): יצא כדרכו, משיצא רוב ראשו; ואיזו רוב ראשו? משתצא פדחתו:
Tosafot on Chullin 68a:8:1.english: The reason is that its head was dead, but if its head were alive, etc. - [This is] astonishing, for [the Gemara] could have raised a difficulty simply from that which [the Mishnah] teaches: "and he is not a firstborn for the priest" — if so, as soon as its head emerged, it is considered like a born child! And one can answer: [it did not ask from that] because one could deflect [it by saying]: what is [meant by] "its head"? Its majority — just as [the Gemara] deflects [it] in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 46b), where Shmuel says: The head does not exempt [a subsequent child from the status of firstborn] in the case of non-viable births; and [the Gemara] raises a difficulty against him from this [clause] of "and he is not a firstborn for the priest," and it answers: What is [meant by] "its head"? Its majority — meaning, its head emerged and its majority also emerged afterward. And [the Gemara there] asks: Then let [the Mishnah] teach "its majority"! And it answers: [The Mishnah] used the term "its head" in order to imply that if its head [emerged] alive, [the one born after it] is not a firstborn even with regard to inheritance. Therefore, the main thrust of its challenge [here] is from this inference. And [the Gemara] could also have raised a difficulty here from the Mishnah in Niddah, as we learned (28a): If it emerged in its normal manner, [it is considered born] once the majority of its head has emerged; and what is [considered] the majority of its head? Once its forehead has emerged:
